raw_segments.text: The most stupid, trivial affair, they made a mountain of a molehill as they always do,"
I was walking through the marketplace here one day just when they'd driven in the geese.
I stopped and looked at them.
All at once a fellow, who is an errand boy at Plotnikov's now, looked at me and said,
"'What are you looking at the geese for?'
He was a stupid, moon-faced fellow of twenty.
I am always on the side of the peasantry, you know.
I like talking to the peasants.
I believe you are laughing, Karamazov.'"
